summary: A genuinely mutual NDA that largely matches the playbook, with possible deviations on the carve-out evidence standard, the combination wording, insurers, compelled-disclosure costs, and an unmapped breach-notification duty.

findings.quote: disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party (the "Receiving Party")
findings.why: Disclosing and Receiving Party are defined so either Party can be either, and the definition protects both.

findings.quote: each Party, acting as the Receiving Party, hereby covenants, undertakes and agrees with the other Party, acting as the Disclosing Party
findings.why: The operative obligations bind each Party equally as Receiving Party.

findings.quote: all information of whatever nature, form or media, whether oral, written, graphic, electronic, machine-readable or tangible
findings.why: The definition is limited to information disclosed in connection with the Purpose and includes derived notes and analyses, though it has no marking or reasonable-confidentiality test.

findings.quote: use the Confidential Information exclusively for the furtherance of the Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, which is a potential commercial transaction and collaboration between the Parties.

findings.quote: can conclusively demonstrate by contemporaneous written records, documentary evidence or other competent proof
findings.why: All four carve-outs are present, but 'conclusively' and 'contemporaneous' set a higher evidence standard than 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence'.
findings.draft_redline: which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like the evidence standard for the exclusions to be written records or other reasonable evidence, as the current wording sets a very high bar for either Party. We hope this is acceptable.

findings.quote: any combination of individual pieces of Confidential Information shall not be deemed to be within the public domain or in the prior possession of the Receiving Party
findings.why: The combination wording further narrows the carve-outs, so a lawyer should confirm whether it is within the same substance as the four standard exclusions.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the second sentence of Clause 3.2 so that the exclusions in Clause 3.1 apply on their ordinary terms.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would prefer to keep the exclusions in Clause 3.1 on their standard terms and so suggest removing the combination wording in Clause 3.2.

findings.quote: the directors, officers, employees, legal advisers, financial auditors, technical consultants, accountants and professional agents of that Party
findings.why: Representatives cover directors, officers, employees, advisers, auditors and Affiliates but do not mention insurers.
findings.draft_redline: "Representatives" means, in relation to a Party, the directors, officers, employees, professional advisers, auditors, insurers and Affiliates of that Party.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to add insurers to the list of permitted Representatives, who remain subject to the same need-to-know and confidentiality obligations.

findings.quote: are bound by written confidentiality obligations or professional duties of secrecy
findings.why: Recipients must be under written confidentiality undertakings or professional duties of secrecy, which is a permitted requirement.
findings.fallback_cited: Requirement for written confidentiality undertakings from advisers who are not under professional duties.

findings.quote: remain fully and unconditionally liable to the Disclosing Party for any breach of the terms of this Agreement caused by any act, omission, default or negligence of any of its Representatives
findings.why: The Receiving Party is liable for its Representatives, as the playbook prefers.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party shall, subject to applicable legal restrictions:
findings.why: Disclosure compelled by law, regulator, court or stock exchange is permitted and notice is qualified by applicable legal restrictions.

findings.quote: exercise all reasonable commercial efforts to obtain a binding written assurance from the presiding court, tribunal or regulatory agency that confidential treatment will be accorded
findings.why: The Receiving Party must use efforts to obtain confidential treatment and fully cooperate, but the clause does not say this is at the Disclosing Party's cost.
findings.draft_redline: exercise reasonable endeavours, at the Disclosing Party's cost, to obtain confidential treatment of the disclosed Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to make clear that the cost of any steps taken to resist or limit a compelled disclosure is borne by the Disclosing Party.

findings.quote: within ten (10) Business Days following receipt of such request
findings.why: Return or destruction within 10 Business Days of written request, as preferred.

findings.quote: a duly authorised officer of the Receiving Party shall provide the Disclosing Party with a written certification
findings.why: Officer-signed written confirmation of compliance is required.

findings.quote: electronic backup copies of Confidential Information generated automatically through routine data archiving, disaster recovery and electronic backup systems
findings.why: Automated backups and a legally required archival copy may be retained and stay confidential under Clause 5.4.

findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as granting, conferring, assigning or transferring, whether expressly, by implication, estoppel or otherwise, any right, title, interest, licence or intellectual property right
findings.why: No assignment or licence is granted and Confidential Information stays with the Disclosing Party.

findings.quote: is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "AS IS" and "AS AVAILABLE" basis, without any representation, warranty or guarantee of any kind
findings.why: Information is provided as is, with no warranty, applying to both Parties.

findings.quote: Neither this Agreement, nor the disclosure or receipt of any Confidential Information, shall constitute, create, imply or evidence an obligation by either Party to enter into any further commercial agreement
findings.why: There is no obligation to proceed and no restriction on either Party's business beyond the confidentiality duties.

findings.quote: reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, decrypt
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: shall immediately notify the Disclosing Party in writing upon becoming aware of any actual, suspected or threatened unauthorised access
findings.why: This mutual duty to notify suspected breaches and cooperate in remedying them is not covered by any playbook rule, so a lawyer should review it.

findings.quote: save for the routine exchange of business contact details
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details.

findings.quote: execute a separate, compliant data processing agreement or data sharing addendum prior to the transfer of any such personal data
findings.why: Any other personal data requires a separate data processing or sharing agreement first.

findings.quote: for a fixed period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: A three-year term with 30 days' notice falls within the 1 to 3 year range.

findings.quote: survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years
findings.why: Five years' survival is within the 2 to 5 year range, with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: the Disclosing Party shall be entitled, without the necessity of posting any bond or other security, and without proving actual damages, to seek and obtain immediate injunctive relief
findings.why: Equitable relief is mutual and strongly worded, with remedies cumulative under Clause 9.3.
findings.fallback_cited: Strongly worded but mutual equitable relief.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer, novate, charge, encumber, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations
findings.why: Neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent.

findings.quote: in accordance with the substantive laws of England and Wales
findings.why: English law governs the Agreement.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: The courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.
